title: Spider mites on African Nightshade, Amaranth and Eggplant

Header: Spider mites on African Nightshade, Amaranth and Eggplant
Tetranychus spp , Mononychellus spp and Oligonychus spp

Prevention: Avoid planting next to infested fields .
Remove and burn infested crop remains immediately after harvest.
Mites favor dry and hot conditions.
Grow healthy plants: avoid water and nutrient stress.
Avoid frequent use of broad-spectrum pesticides, in particular pyrethroids; this may lead to spider mite outbreaks.
Rotate crop with non-host plants such as maize, pulses or chive.
Monitoring: Spider mites which look like tiny, moving dots, mostly on the undersides of leaves.
Symptoms appear first on leaves becoming stippled with tiny light spots.
Web formation on plants indicates severe infestation.
Later, the leaves often take on a bronze colour and have a dusty, dry appearance.
Finally, the leaves turn yellow or red, dry up and fall off
Direct Control: Malathion – 3 table spoonful in 1 gallon of water and apply using a sprayer.
Use overhead irrigation or wash plants with a strong jet of water to knock off mites and destroy their webs.
Be sure to spray the underneath of the leaves.
Mix 2½ table spoonful of liquid soap to a gallon of water.
Apply underneath the leaves. spray in the morning or late afternoon

Some pesticides can kill natural pest enemies and thus increase mite population.
Care should be taken to avoid this.
